proxy.role: proxy under test, one core (CPU 0, its hyperthread sibling offline, NIC interrupts moved to the other cores)

origin_sink.role: static origin (8 threads) and discard sink (8 threads)

network.kind: 25 Gbit/s Private Network (VLAN on the NIC)

limits.text: The origin is static with Content-Length. Chunked bodies, uploads, SOCKS5, IPv6, many origins and large header sets are not part of the matrix; they are covered functionally by the end-to-end suite.
One campaign, one seed, three repeats, medians, noise about ±3 to 5 %, no confidence intervals. Differences below the noise are not conclusions.
Latency is closed-loop at each concurrency level (no open-loop rate); CPU per request is measured at saturation, not at an equal offered load.
The 25 Gbit/s link (23.5 measured) is a ceiling: a proxy that reaches it (rustle at 1 MB, 10 MB and in plain tunnels) shows the link, not its own limit, and its figure is a lower bound.
There is no splice on a TLS port (the proxy decrypts in user space), so TLS and HTTP/2 throughput is lower than plain HTTP.
The HTTP/2 test opens one connection per client connection and sends sequential requests (no multiplexing).
Multi-core was measured for plain HTTP at 1 KB only; TLS, HTTP/2 and tunnels were not measured on several cores.
Proxy CPU is the container cgroup's (user + system); softirq time spent on other cores is not attributed.
The tunnel test counts bytes written by the client and measures the upload direction only.

test_notes.plain-1mb: rustle is at 95 % of its core, near the link ceiling: its lead is a lower bound.
test_notes.plain-10mb: rustle is at 83 % of its core, at the link ceiling (about 22 of 23.5 Gbit/s): its figure is a lower bound.
test_notes.plain-flood: rustle is at 70 % of its core, at the link ceiling (about 22 of 23.5 Gbit/s): its figure is a lower bound.
test_notes.tls-short-full: Session resumption is off: every connection is a full handshake with the certificate signature.
test_notes.ws-short: Tinyproxy removes the Upgrade header (answered 426): it does not support WebSocket and is listed as unsupported, not as zero.
